headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad API/network defaults can exfiltrate or mis-handle ComfyUI outputs, while ComfyUI’s offline design limits direct injection risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI has no browser, stdin/stdout, clipboard, or MCP surfaces, and RD-Agent’s documented inputs are APIs/files rather than a direct shared channel. A prompt-injection bridge is therefore not default. The remaining pathway is unusual manual handoff of ComfyUI outputs into RD-Agent prompts, so risk stays low.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies ComfyUI-generated text into RD-Agent prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared message queue or file bridge is added between the agents, the pathway opens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste model outputs into RD-Agent prompts without review.
Disable any ad hoc clipboard-based handoff.
Use a fixed template for RD-Agent inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for any bridged content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches workflows, seeds, checkpoints, embeddings, and other local model assets, while RD-Agent handles logs and sends data to external APIs by default. Even without a shared filesystem, any operator-mediated transfer of ComfyUI artifacts into RD-Agent can leak sensitive model assets or workflow details to third-party inference backends.
conditions: IF ComfyUI workflows or checkpoints are copied into RD-Agent inputs, those contents can leave the local environment.
IF RD-Agent is configured with external API keys, transferred content may be sent off-box.
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI artifacts out of RD-Agent prompts.
Use redacted summaries instead of raw files.
Rotate any API keys used by RD-Agent.
Restrict RD-Agent to non-sensitive datasets.
requires-engineering: enforce content filters before API calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, and RD-Agent’s documented surfaces are API calls plus log files. There is little direct write-write overlap, so conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because RD-Agent supports multiple instances and external APIs, but no shared mutable resource is documented here.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same log directory, file contention can occur.
IF an operator mounts a shared writable workspace for both agents, conflicts increase.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Avoid sharing git repositories between them.
Serialize any writes to common logs.
Run one instance per workspace.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent is a research automation system with browser and API access, so it can treat upstream outputs as actionable inputs. ComfyUI can generate workflows and assets that RD-Agent may summarize or operationalize. Without an explicit verification step, errors in ComfyUI outputs can cascade into RD-Agent’s downstream actions or reports.
conditions: IF RD-Agent consumes ComfyUI-generated text or metadata as authoritative, errors propagate.
IF RD-Agent is allowed to act on those outputs without human review, downstream mistakes can occur.
mitigations: Require human review before RD-Agent acts on ComfyUI outputs.
Mark ComfyUI outputs as untrusted in prompts.
Use a verification checklist for any derived claims.
Limit RD-Agent to summarization only.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates.

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI is offline-first and local, while RD-Agent explicitly uses third-party APIs and handles secrets such as OpenAI and Azure keys. If regulated or sensitive data from ComfyUI workflows is routed into RD-Agent, residency and retention obligations can diverge. The other agent is cited because the compliance risk arises from their interaction.
conditions: IF EU PII or other regulated data from ComfyUI is sent into RD-Agent APIs, residency/compliance issues arise.
IF retention policies differ between local ComfyUI artifacts and RD-Agent logs, compliance gaps appear.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of RD-Agent inputs.
Use a data-classification checklist before transfer.
Disable logging of sensitive prompts.
Confirm vendor DPAs before use.
requires-engineering: implement retention and residency controls.
